title: Hunt the hidden boxing
prompt: Implement `static long SumInterface(IEnumerable<int> values)` (sums via foreach over the interface — allocates an enumerator + boxes if you use a struct enumerator through IEnumerable) and `static long SumSpan(int[] values)` (sums via Span<int> — zero allocations). The test proves the allocation gap: SumSpan must allocate 0 over 100 runs; SumInterface's cost is printed for comparison. Implement both, correctly, and the numbers teach the lesson.

tests.name: values-match
tests.hint: foreach over array via IEnumerable boxes an IEnumerator<int>; span foreach uses ref iteration.

tests.name: span-zero-alloc
tests.hint: foreach (var v in values.AsSpan()) — no enumerator object exists at all.
